package_info.package_manager: system/library (various, e.g., apt, yum, Homebrew, Maven Central wrappers)
package_info.why_malicious: OpenSSL versions 3.0.0 through 3.0.6 contain a critical security vulnerability (CVE-2022-3602 and CVE-2022-3786) that allows attackers to exploit buffer overflows during X.509 certificate verification, potentially leading to remote code execution or denial of service. This vulnerability can compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of systems relying on OpenSSL for cryptographic operations. The issue is resolved in version 3.0.7.

behavioral_signatures: Detection of applications or services performing cryptographic operations using OpenSSL versions 3.0.0 through 3.0.6.
Processes dynamically or statically linking to vulnerable OpenSSL 3.0.0 - 3.0.6 libraries.
Abnormal process crashes or memory corruption during TLS/SSL handshake or certificate validation, especially when handling untrusted certificates.
file_indicators: Presence of libssl.so.3.0.0, libssl.so.3.0.1, libssl.so.3.0.2, libssl.so.3.0.3, libssl.so.3.0.4, libssl.so.3.0.5, or libssl.so.3.0.6 on disk.
Presence of OpenSSL 3.0.0 - 3.0.6 libraries in /usr/lib, /usr/local/lib, or application-specific directories.
Maven Central Java wrapper packages (e.g., org.openssl:openssl) bundling OpenSSL 3.0.0 - 3.0.6.
network_indicators: No direct network IOCs; however, exploitation attempts may result in abnormal TLS/SSL handshake failures, unexpected process terminations, or memory access violations observable in logs.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Perform automated scans of all systems and application dependencies to identify OpenSSL versions 3.0.0 through 3.0.6, including both dynamically and statically linked libraries. Check for the presence of vulnerable library files in standard and non-standard locations. Review dependency manifests (e.g., Maven, package.json, requirements.txt) for references to affected versions. Monitor system and application logs for abnormal TLS/SSL handshake failures, process crashes, or memory corruption events during certificate validation. Use vulnerability management tools to flag and prioritize patching of affected systems.
